doc.name: A — mechanical keyboard catalogue, sand dune, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: 65 percent hot-swap keyboard
Category: mechanical keyboard
Shot programme: sand dune
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this mechanical keyboard product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the back-label view in a sand dune treatment.

SUBJECT. A 65 percent hot-swap keyboard. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Rotated to show the reverse face, ingredient panel or hardware detail. Shoot on a 58mm vintage double-gauss at f/8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a book light bounce producing an extremely soft wrap. Stage the product on or against cracked dry clay, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
